name: Comparison edits (phonk)

lead: Comparison edits are short videos that put a person's older and newer appearance next to each other, or in sequence, set to energetic phonk, a bass-heavy music style. In looksmaxxing they serve as a way to show changes from grooming, fitness, skin care or surgery.
Phonk began in the early 2010s in the US and a faster drift phonk variant spread through TikTok from 2020, where it is widely used for weightlifting, fighting and car videos, per Wikipedia.

paras: Creators cut clips or photos from different stages, time them to beat drops and post to short-video platforms. The format is mainly for sharing progress and drawing views.
No physical risk. Selective angles, lighting and editing can shape how a comparison appears.

angle.text: The edits do not change appearance themselves; they document and publicise changes made by other means, giving viewers visual examples of what grooming, training or procedures can look like.

lead: A comparison edit is a short video that shows how a person's appearance has changed, typically timed to music. Phonk, a genre that Wikipedia says grew from Memphis rap influences and was popularised by SpaceGhostPurrp around 2012, is a common soundtrack [1].

The drift phonk subgenre, with fast tempos, heavy bass and cowbell sounds, spread through TikTok from 2020 and is often used in videos about weightlifting, fighting sports, football and cars [1]. That fit with high-energy short clips is part of why the style is associated with transformation edits.

paras: Phonk's rise: it emerged from SoundCloud in the early 2010s, and drift phonk, originating in Russia in the late 2010s, expanded on TikTok from 2020 [1]. Wikipedia says the genre became associated with scrolling through short-video feeds [1].

timeline.event: SpaceGhostPurrp releases Mysterious Phonk, helping define the genre [1].
